answer: Pay each agent by its leave-one-out value: how much the pooled forecast worsens when that agent's input is removed. Say agents predict, over a ten-day horizon, when melt will swell a tundra river, or how far a desert oasis well will drop. An independent agent with its own data shifts the pool; remove it and accuracy falls, so it earns. Three hundred clones echoing one model add nothing apiece, since removing any one leaves its twins saying the same thing, so the farm splits about zero.
